result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had a review on 30 September 2026. Your asthma is flaring up. You have been prescribed prednisolone tablets. This is a steroid medicine. The tablets are 5 milligrams each. You will take a reducing dose. You will take it for 11 days, then stop.

## What you need to do
1. Take prednisolone tablets every morning with food. Follow the dose schedule below.
2. Keep taking your usual inhalers.
3. Carry the blue steroid card. The pharmacy will give it to you.
4. Book a review with the asthma nurse. Do this within 2 weeks, by 14 October 2026.

## Dates and medicines

Prednisolone tablets:
- 1 October to 5 October 2026: 40 milligrams (8 tablets) each day, in the morning with food
- 6 October to 8 October 2026: 20 milligrams (4 tablets) each day, in the morning with food
- 9 October to 11 October 2026: 10 milligrams (2 tablets) each day, in the morning with food
- 12 October 2026: stop taking prednisolone

Asthma nurse review: by 14 October 2026

## Questions to ask your doctor
1. What should I do if I still feel unwell after the prednisolone finishes?
2. When should I feel better?
3. Should I adjust any of my other inhalers?

## When to get urgent help
If your breathing gets worse, call 999. If your reliever inhaler does not help, call 999.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
